legend_snippet: a, Age at diagnosis, tumor sequencing depth and tumor purity across TCGA-THCA (n = 455), Chornobyl-unexposed (n = 70) and Chornobyl-exposed (n = 283) tumors. Box plots show the median (center line), interquartile range (box) and whiskers extending to 1.5× the interquartile range.
b, Cohort-specific mutation frequencies of driver genes identified by IntOGen, coloured by predicted mode of action (activating, ambiguous or loss of function).
c, Structural-variant breakpoint density per sample in 5-Mb genomic windows across the three cohorts. Recurrent peaks overlapping major kinase genes are labelled.
d–f, Circos plots showing structural variants in TCGA-THCA (d), Chornobyl-unexposed (e) and Chornobyl-exposed (f) tumors.
d–f, Circos plots showing structural variants in TCGA-THCA (d), Chornobyl-unexposed (e) and Chornobyl-exposed (f) tumors.
d–f, Circos plots showing structural variants in TCGA-THCA (d), Chornobyl-unexposed (e) and Chornobyl-exposed (f) tumors.

g–i, Integrated genomic profiles of driver mutations, oncogenic fusions, TERT-promoter mutations and clonal or subclonal 22q loss in TCGA-THCA (g), Chornobyl-exposed (h) and Chornobyl-unexposed (i) tumors. Bars above each oncoprint indicate sample-level mutation burden; percentages at right indicate cohort-specific frequencies of individual alterations.

g–i, Integrated genomic profiles of driver mutations, oncogenic fusions, TERT-promoter mutations and clonal or subclonal 22q loss in TCGA-THCA (g), Chornobyl-exposed (h) and Chornobyl-unexposed (i) tumors. Bars above each oncoprint indicate sample-level mutation burden; percentages at right indicate cohort-specific frequencies of individual alterations.

g–i, Integrated genomic profiles of driver mutations, oncogenic fusions, TERT-promoter mutations and clonal or subclonal 22q loss in TCGA-THCA (g), Chornobyl-exposed (h) and Chornobyl-unexposed (i) tumors. Bars above each oncoprint indicate sample-level mutation burden; percentages at right indicate cohort-specific frequencies of individual alterations.

a, Genome-wide frequencies of clonal (top) and subclonal (bottom) somatic copy-number gains, losses, amplifications and homozygous deletions inferred using Battenberg. Chromosome boundaries are indicated.
b, Copy-number states across chromosome 22q in tumors with clonal or subclonal 22q loss, grouped by cohort.

c, Estimated cancer cell fraction (CCF) of subclonal 22q loss across the three cohorts. Points represent individual tumors. Box plots show the median (center line), interquartile range (box) and whiskers extending to 1.5× the interquartile range.

d, Associations of clonal (left) and subclonal (right) 22q loss with recurrent mutations and oncogenic fusions. The x axes show log2 odds ratios and the y axes show −log10(FDR) from two-sided Fisher’s exact tests. Events with FDR < 0.05 are labelled.
a, Ridgeline distributions of MATH scores across the three cohorts; vertical lines indicate cohort medians.

b, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with MATH score in the combined cohort. The x axis shows the log2 fold change in MATH between alteration-positive and alteration-negative tumors, and the y axis shows −log10(FDR). The horizontal dotted line denotes FDR = 0.05.
c, MATH score distributions stratified by TERT-promoter mutation, BRAF mutation, KRAS mutation and clonal 22q-loss status.

d, Minimum CCF of detected mutation clusters as a function of the number of reads per tumor chromosomal copy (NRPCC). Each point represents one tumor and colour indicates the number of inferred subclones; marginal CCF distributions are shown at right.
e, Distribution of the number of detected subclones across major genomic alteration groups. Counts are shown within bars.

a, Distributions of inferred CCFs for clonal and subclonal mutation clusters across the three cohorts. Dashed lines indicate the recurrent subclonal peak at CCF 0.20–0.25 and the clonal peak near 1.0.

b, Relationship between CCF and the proportion of mutations assigned to each cluster, stratified by cohort and subclonal mutation-burden state. Red points denote clonal clusters; cyan and green points denote mutation-rich and mutation-poor subclonal clusters, respectively; point size represents the proportion of mutations assigned to each cluster.
c, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with high versus low subclonal mutation burden in the combined cohort.

d, Corresponding associations within each cohort. In c,d, the x axes show log2 odds ratios from Fisher’s exact tests and the y axes show −log10(P values). Horizontal dashed lines denote P < 0.05 (lower) and FDR < 0.05 (upper); alterations with P < 0.05 are labelled.

e, Schematic phylogenetic trees illustrating a BRAF-associated architecture characterized by mutation-rich subclonal expansion, with subclonal 22q loss in a subset of tumors (top), and a clonal-dominant architecture associated with KRAS, TERT-promoter mutation, oncogenic fusions or clonal 22q loss, including BRAF plus TERT tumors (bottom). Schematics summarize recurrent associations and do not imply a fixed order of evolutionary events.

a, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with age at diagnosis, age at exposure and radiation dose. The x axis shows the effect estimate and the y axis shows −log10(FDR); symbol shape denotes alteration type and colour denotes the age or exposure variable.
b–d, Age-stratified frequencies of TERT-promoter mutation (b), BRAF mutation (c) and oncogenic fusions (d) by cohort. Point size indicates the number of tumors in each age group.
b–d, Age-stratified frequencies of TERT-promoter mutation (b), BRAF mutation (c) and oncogenic fusions (d) by cohort. Point size indicates the number of tumors in each age group.
b–d, Age-stratified frequencies of TERT-promoter mutation (b), BRAF mutation (c) and oncogenic fusions (d) by cohort. Point size indicates the number of tumors in each age group.

e, Associations of clinical, ancestry and exposure variables with inferred tumor latency combined cohorts. Points and error bars show regression coefficients and confidence intervals, respectively; β coefficients and P values are shown.
f, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with inferred tumor latency.

g, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with inferred age at the most recent common ancestor (MRCA). In f and g, the x axis shows the regression coefficient and the y axis shows −log10(FDR). Dashed lines denote FDR = 0.05.

a, Clonal SBS1 plus SBS5 mutation burden as a function of age at diagnosis in TCGA-THCA. Segmented regression identified a breakpoint at 52.2 years (95% confidence interval, 45.8–58.7 years), with age-associated slopes of 4.7 ± 1.5 mutations per year before and 15.8 ± 1.8 mutations per year after the breakpoint. Red-inlined points indicate tumors harboring TERT-promoter mutations.

b, Corresponding relationship in the combined Chornobyl cohorts, with an age-associated linear slope of 4.6 mutations per year. Points represent individual tumors and shaded bands indicate uncertainty around the fitted regression lines.

Extended Data Fig. 1: Genomic alteration burden across PTC WGS cohorts. Tumor mutation burden (TMB; mutations per megabase), percentage of genome altered (PGA), number of structural-variant (SV) events and number of transposable-element (TE) events across the three cohorts. SV and TE counts are shown on a log2 scale. Points represent individual tumors; box plots show the median (center line), interquartile range (box) and whiskers extending to 1.5× the interquartile range. FDR-adjusted P values for the indicated cohort comparisons are shown above brackets.

a, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with MATH score within each cohort. The x axes show log2 fold changes in MATH between alteration-positive and alteration-negative tumors, and the y axes show −log10(P values); colours denote alteration type.

b, MATH score distributions stratified by TERT-promoter mutation, BRAF mutation, KRAS mutation and clonal 22q-loss status within each cohort. Points represent individual tumors; box plots show the median and interquartile range.

a,b, Variant-allele fraction and estimated cancer cell fraction (CCF), together with CCF distributions of fitted mutation clusters, for two representative PTC tumors. Colours distinguish inferred mutation clusters, and annotations indicate cluster CCFs and numbers of assigned mutations. | a, Example of a tumor with a predominantly clonal mutation burden (TCGA-EL-A3H3-01A-11D-A85S-36).

a,b, Variant-allele fraction and estimated cancer cell fraction (CCF), together with CCF distributions of fitted mutation clusters, for two representative PTC tumors. Colours distinguish inferred mutation clusters, and annotations indicate cluster CCFs and numbers of assigned mutations. | b, Example of a tumor with a mutation-rich subclonal population (TCGA-EM-A3FJ-01A-11D-A85U-36).
a, Estimated age at the most recent common ancestor (MRCA) in tumors classified as other, BRAF only, BRAF plus TERT-promoter mutation or TERT-promoter mutation only.

b, Age at diagnosis across the same groups. In a,b, points represent individual tumors and box plots show the median (center line), interquartile range (box) and whiskers extending to 1.5× the interquartile range; FDR-adjusted P values for the indicated pairwise comparisons are shown.
c, Prevalence of APOBEC mutagenesis across TERT-only, other, BRAF-only and BRAF plus TERT tumors. APOBEC mutagenesis was detected in 9.1%, 11.9%, 21.8% and 39.0% of tumors, respectively.

a–c, Genome-wide LogR, B-allele frequency (BAF), allele-specific absolute copy number and segment cancer cell fraction (CCF) for three representative tumors. Orange and green lines denote total and minor copy number of the major clone, respectively; additional colours indicate subclonal copy-number states. Sample-level purity, ploidy and percentage of genome altered are shown below each profile.

Supplementary Fig. 2: Minimum detected CCF across genomic alteration groups. Density distributions of the minimum detected CCF across recurrent genomic alteration groups.

a, Associations of recurrent genomic alterations with MATH score within each cohort. The x axes show log2 fold changes in MATH between alteration-positive and alteration-negative tumors, and the y axes show −log10(P values). Colours denote alteration type; the horizontal dashed line denotes P = 0.05. Alterations with significant associations are labelled.

b, MATH score distributions stratified by TERT-promoter mutation, BRAF mutation, KRAS mutation and clonal 22q-loss status within each cohort. Violin plots show the distribution of MATH scores, with embedded box plots indicating the median and interquartile range.
